evals.prompt: We use flagd. Write me a flags.flagd.json with three flags: (1) `new-checkout` boolean, rolled out to 20% of users by targetingKey but always on for anyone with an @acme.io email; (2) `pricing-tier` string with variants basic/pro/enterprise chosen by the `plan` context attribute, default basic; (3) `min-app-version-gate` boolean that is on only when context `appVersion` is >= 2.3.0 semver. Then show the curl command to verify flag 1 for user u-123 with email bob@acme.io against a local flagd.
evals.expected_output: A single valid flagd JSON file using $schema, fractional with weights summing to 100 (or equivalent), ends_with on email, sem_ver >= operator, targeting returning variant names; plus a correct curl to :8013 Connect (flagd.evaluation.v2.Service/ResolveBoolean) or :8016 OFREP with the right ports and body.
assertions: flags.flagd.json is valid JSON with top-level `flags` and all three keys new-checkout, pricing-tier, min-app-version-gate
new-checkout targeting uses the `fractional` operator with weights giving ~20% to the on variant (e.g. ["on",20],["off",80])
new-checkout checks email with `ends_with` on `@acme.io` before the fractional split, returning variant "on"
pricing-tier defaultVariant is basic and targeting maps context `plan` to a variant NAME (basic/pro/enterprise), not to a value
min-app-version-gate uses `sem_ver` with operator `>=` against `appVersion` and value 2.3.0
All targeting rules return variant names (strings that are keys of `variants`), never raw true/false values
curl targets a correct flagd endpoint and port: :8016 /ofrep/v1/evaluate/flags/new-checkout or :8013 /flagd.evaluation.v2.Service/ResolveBoolean (v1 acceptable), POST with JSON body
curl body includes targetingKey u-123 and email bob@acme.io in the evaluation context
File includes the $schema https://flagd.dev/schema/v0/flags.json line

evals.prompt: I have a FastAPI service and want self-hosted feature flags with OpenFeature. Set up flagd next to it in docker-compose (flags in ./flags), and write the Python code to init the flagd provider in RPC mode, evaluate a boolean flag `beta-dashboard` for a user in a request handler, and read flagd host/port from env. Also explain briefly when I'd switch to in-process mode.
evals.expected_output: docker-compose with ghcr.io/open-feature/flagd image, start --uri file:..., port 8013 exposed; pip install openfeature-sdk openfeature-provider-flagd; FlagdProvider(host=..., port=8013) via api.set_provider; get_client().get_boolean_value with EvaluationContext(targeting_key=...); mentions FLAGD_HOST/FLAGD_PORT; correct in-process explanation (sync :8015 / offline file).
assertions: docker-compose uses image ghcr.io/open-feature/flagd with `start --uri file:...` pointing at a mounted ./flags file and exposes port 8013
Python uses the real packages: openfeature-sdk (`from openfeature import api`) and openfeature-provider-flagd (`from openfeature.contrib.provider.flagd import FlagdProvider`)
Provider is registered via api.set_provider(FlagdProvider(...)) with host/port coming from environment (explicit os.environ reads or documented FLAGD_HOST/FLAGD_PORT auto-read)
Request handler evaluates `beta-dashboard` with client.get_boolean_value(...) passing an EvaluationContext that includes targeting_key
Answer explains in-process mode correctly: provider pulls flag config over the sync service (port 8015) or from a local file and evaluates locally; motivates by latency / no per-call network hop
Provides a sample flags file for beta-dashboard consistent with flagd schema (state, variants, defaultVariant)
If port numbers for OFREP/management are given, they are correct (OFREP 8016, management 8014, sync 8015)
Does not invent nonexistent APIs (wrong module paths, wrong class names, FlagdProvider(url=...))

evals.prompt: Our Java service's flagd in-process provider connects fine (PROVIDER_READY fires) but every flag evaluates to the code default with reason DEFAULT or FLAG_NOT_FOUND. flagd runs with two --uri file sources and we added `metadata.flagSetId: "payments"` to one file last week. What's wrong and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses selector/flag-set mismatch: in-process provider must set selector `flagSetId=payments` (FLAGD_SOURCE_SELECTOR / .selector()) or flags without matching flagSetId are filtered; mentions checking curl :8015/v1/flags with Flagd-Selector header, reason DEFAULT vs FLAG_NOT_FOUND distinction, and the migrating-to-flag-sets guide.
assertions: Diagnoses the root cause as flag-set / selector mismatch: after adding metadata.flagSetId the flags belong to flag set `payments` and the in-process provider's selector must match (flags in the other file stay in the default/null set)
Gives the concrete fix for the Java provider: FlagdOptions.builder().selector("flagSetId=payments") or env FLAGD_SOURCE_SELECTOR=flagSetId=payments
Explains the distinction between reason DEFAULT (flag found, no targeting match / null default) and FLAG_NOT_FOUND (flag not in the selected set)
Gives a verification command against the sync endpoint, e.g. curl -H 'Flagd-Selector: flagSetId=payments' http://localhost:8015/v1/flags or grpcurl FetchAllFlags with selector
Mentions that flags from the second file (without flagSetId) will not be visible under the payments selector, and offers adding the same flagSetId to both files (or a second provider) as the remedy
Does not misattribute the problem to RPC-mode settings, port 8013, or targeting rules
All cited ports are correct: 8013 evaluation, 8014 management, 8015 sync, 8016 OFREP (OFREP on 8014 fails)
